sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1984. A Mussau vocabulary, with phonological notes. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 23, Pacific Linguistics A-69:159-208.
sources.note: For MUSSAU (not Tenis): sec. 2.4.2 p.173 'In the great majority of cases primary stress was recorded on the penultimate vocoid.. primary stress can be assigned to the penultimate mora of the word', with stress shift under suffixation (2.4.3). On Tenis only p.159: 'Lithgow and Claassen (1968) offer a few passing observations on the phonetic typology of Musau, Emira and Tenis.'
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 23, Pacific Linguistics A-69:159-208

sources.citation: Vogel(-Hamburg), Hans. 1911. Eine Forschungsreise im Bismarck-Archipel. Hamburg: L. Friederichsen. (archive.org scanned text, id eineforschungsre00voge)
sources.note: Ch. 3 'Tench-Insel' (pp.67ff) is expedition narrative of the 1908 landing on Tench; a full-text search for stress/accent Sprache/Betonung/Akzent finds no language notes on Tench.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2019. Ethnologue 22nd ed., entry Tenis [tns] (Internet Archive copy 2019)
sources.note: No structural information; 30 speakers (Wurm 2000), shifting to Mussau-Emira and Tok Pisin.

sources.citation: Parkinson, Richard. 2010 [German original 1907]. Thirty Years in the South Seas: Land and People, Customs and Traditions in the Bismarck Archipelago and on the German Solomon Islands (transl. J. Dennison). Chapter 3: St Matthias and the Neighbouring Islands. Sydney: Sydney University Press. (hdl 2123/7036)
sources.note: Ethnographic narrative; the only remarks on the Tench language (printed p.151): 'Unfortunately we could not understand a word; neither could the St Matthias people nor the New Ireland and New Hanover natives on board understand a single syllable of the language. This was very rich in vowels, and almost every sentence ended in a long, drawn-out ma or ha'. No statement on stress, accent or tone; no wordlist.

sources.citation: Brownie, John & Marjo Brownie. 2007. Mussau Grammar Essentials. Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages 52. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG Academic Publications. iv+221 pp.
sources.note: For MUSSAU-EMIRA (not Tenis): sec. 2.5 pp.21-22 'Stress is specified lexically, but generally falls on the penultimate syllable of the word, with secondary stress on every second syllable before the primary stress. A long vowel in the final syllable shifts the stress to the final syllable.' Tenis mentioned only in sec. 1.3 (p.4) as the other St Matthias language, ~50 speakers; no Tenis data.
sources.venue: Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2002. Mussau. In Lynch, Ross & Crowley (eds.), The Oceanic Languages, 148-166. Richmond: Curzon.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Mussau only; on Tenis says 'The other is Tench (or Tenis), for which we have almost no data, but which appears to be quite closely related to Mussau (Beaumont 1976).' No Tenis prosody.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. xiii+487 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing on Tench/Tenis prosody. Tench appears only in ch. 9 consonant-correspondence Table 36 (p.321) and cognate sets; Appendix B names the sole Tench data source as 'Lithgow and Claassen 1968'.

sources.citation: Beaumont, C.H. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, Pacific Linguistics C-39:387-397.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Tenis appears in the subgroup list, the map, six items of the comparative vocabulary, and one segmental remark (p.391: for POc *l 'Emira-Mussau and Tenis appear to vary, with r being the most common').
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Beaumont, C.H. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 171-177. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/252994)
sources.note: No prosody for any St Matthias variety. Relevant only for calibrating the list of works to obtain: 'there have been two general surveys carried out by A. Capell in 1952 and by D. Lithgow and Oren Claassen of the Summer Institute of Linguistics in 1966.. Lithgow and Claassen (1968) made some lexicostatistical comparisons of the languages. Their work is brief but it is very useful for establishing the language boundaries, and it has good language maps.' Conclusions (p.174): 'Even extensive word lists are not generally available.'
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Beaumont, C.H. 1972. New Ireland languages: a review. In Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3, Pacific Linguistics A-35:1-41.
sources.note: Sec. 1.4 reviews phonetic notes for New Ireland languages (stops, fricatives, vowels, tone in Kara/Barok) from Lithgow & Claassen and mission grammars; nothing on stress for Emira-Mussau or Tenis. Sec. 1.2.10.6 places Emira-Mussau and Tenis in a St Matthias subgroup on lexicostatistics.
sources.venue: Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3, Pacific Linguistics A-35:1-41

sources.citation: Nevermann, Hans. 1933. St. Matthias-Gruppe. Ergebnisse der Suedsee-Expedition 1908-1910, II. Ethnographie: A. Melanesien, Band 2. Hamburg: Friederichsen, de Gruyter. xvi+250 pp.
sources.note: Hamburg expedition ethnography of the St Matthias group listed by Glottolog under Tenis; may contain a Tench vocabulary or language notes (German). Not online in full view.

sources.citation: [Anon.] 1914. Tench-Insel (Enus). Deutsche Kolonialzeitung 31(3): 38 (17 Januar 1914); reprint of the report in Amtsblatt fuer das Schutzgebiet Deutsch-Neuguinea 5 (1913): 247 on the government steamer Komet's visit to Tench, 14 August 1913. (Cited by Riesenfeld 1950 as Schnee 1914 'Die Tench Insel (Enus)'.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. The only linguistic content is one sentence on intelligibility/relatedness: a Mussau speaker from Tatitel picked out familiar words and found the Tench speech very similar to that of Emirau, itself a dialect of the St Matthias language; the islanders call their island Enus and say they were drifted there from Emirau. One local plant name (aisacka, given as the St Matthias word). Rest is settlement, houses, material culture.

sources.citation: Parkinson, Richard. 1905. St. Matthias und die Inseln Kerué und Tench. Globus 88(5): 69-72. Braunschweig.
sources.note: No phonology content. On Tench: 'Eine Verständigung war unmöglich, weder die Sprache von St. Matthias noch von Neu-Hannover und Neu-Mecklenburg war ihnen bekannt.' On Emirau: 'Die Sprache der Bewohner ist dieselbe wie die der St. Matthias-Insulaner'. Rest is material culture and discovery history.
